report.scope: Daily-wear facial sunscreens from Japanese brands (Biore, Anessa, Skin Aqua, Senka and similar), bought as US imports. Body-only, Korean and US-made 'Japanese-style' products excluded.

primer.what_it_is: Cosmetic-feeling chemical (organic-filter) essences, gels and milks for daily wear under makeup, at SPF 50+ and PA++++ (Japan's UVA rating). Not sold in US drugstores under US drug rules, so imported.

must_haves.why: Top of the Japanese scale, but manufacturer self-reported; the filter system matters more than the label
Dominant factor for daily users; sticky or pilling products get skipped
Anessa is heavily counterfeited; Skin Aqua has 16 versions and the Chinese one differs from the Japanese

must_haves.feature: Properly dosed application (~1.25 g face and neck)
must_haves.why: Labelled SPF assumes about 2 mg/cm²; under-applying cuts protection (working assumption, not tested)

premium_features.why: Hides white cast; adds refinement, not meaningfully more protection
For reapplying over makeup, not as a base layer

avoid.thing: Marketplace prices far below specialist price (esp. Anessa)
avoid.why: Warning sign of fake or old stock, not a bargain
eBay Biore 4-pack at $50.99 (~$12.75 each) costs more than YesStyle's $10.22 tube
More than double Biore's price for an unproven edge; no independent testing found
Feels like makeup, so under-application is common

verdict.headline: Buy Biore UV Aqua Rich around $10; add Anessa only for outdoor days.
verdict.confidence: Low-moderate: partial price snapshot, no lab tests, no price history, some sizes unconfirmed
verdict.reasoning: Biore at $10.22 sits at the knee and has broad community validation. Pricier options mostly add outdoor film, tone-up, powder and brand, not better desk-and-commute protection. Beware counterfeits, variant mismatches and fake 'sale' discounts.
verdict.price_watch_summary: YesStyle's '30% off' is the permanent street price (Biore list $14.60, sold $10.22). Buy-under: Biore $10.50 per tube, above $13 is overpaying. Anessa $16.63 rarely discounts (~5%), so buy when needed. No price history seen; cadence inferred.

normalization.unit: Cost per properly dosed face-and-neck application (1.25 g)
normalization.unit_rationale: Tubes range from about 40 g to 90 g or more, and texture changes how much people apply. Per-gram or per-tube price misleads. 1.25 g is a working assumption (roughly 1.2–1.5 g), not confirmed in testing.
normalization.quality_adjustment: Effective cost = cost per dosed application ÷ (UVA performance × wearability × authenticity confidence), each factor 0 to 1. Wearability dominates for daily users; authenticity matters most for Anessa.
normalization.formula: effective cost = cost per dosed application ÷ (UVA performance × wearability × authenticity confidence)

normalization.size_economics: Biore 70 g at $10.22 gives ~56 applications (~$0.18). Skin Aqua Tone Up 80 g at $12.99 gives ~64 (~$0.20). From memory, unconfirmed: Anessa gel 90 g, Senka 70 g, Canmake ~40 g. Check listings.

diminishing_returns.knee_example: Biore UV Aqua Rich 70 g at $10.22 (YesStyle), about $0.18 per application, is the benchmark.
diminishing_returns.below_knee: You give up either size or a good formula. Canmake Mermaid Skin Gel at $8.40 looks cheap but is a smaller tube, and lacks Biore's broad community validation.
diminishing_returns.above_knee: Extra money buys mainly Anessa's stronger sweat- and water-activated film, tone-up and skincare layers, powder formats, and refinement and brand. For desk-and-commute wear, none buy meaningfully better protection.

consensus.expert_view: Dermatologists and regulators note US and Japanese filters differ and popular Japanese products are not FDA-labelled OTC drugs. No independent lab measurement of any product was found, so actual SPF is unconfirmed.
consensus.community_view: Enthusiasts favour Biore for cosmetic elegance and daily use; Anessa and Allie for sweat and outdoor use. One poster with 9 years of use likes Anessa and Allie for oily skin and humid climates. Snippets only; originals not read.
consensus.where_they_disagree: Skeptics (Reddit snippet, unread) say Japan's SPF/PA testing isn't identical to US testing, so numbers aren't strictly comparable; enthusiasts rely on the labels and daily-wear experience.
